answers: One of the most renowned hairstylists in Los Angeles was murdered on Monday by intruders who made their getaway in his Porsche, police say. Fabio Sementilli was stabbed several times and was found on his home's patio by his wife and daughter, CBS Los Angeles reports. Paramedics were called but the 49-year-old was bleeding profusely and died at the scene. Police say the Canadian-born hairstylist's 2008 Porsche 911 Carrera was missing from the scene and they believe it was stolen by two men who broke into the upscale Woodland Hills home and attacked Sementilli. Police aren't sure whether the murder was random or a targeted attack, the AP reports. Sementilli gained international recognition during his 30 years as a hairstylist and also served as an exec at companies including Wella, the Los Angeles Daily News reports. He was "recognized as an exceptional stylist, educator, and visionary," Wella said in a statement that describes him as "an icon in the hairdressing industry." A post at Modern Salon says he was a VP of education for cosmetics company Coty, adding that he "mentored tens of thousands of hairdressers with a hands-on approach either on a one-to-one basis or on a grander scale." (This man was murdered just two months after President Obama commuted his sentence.)

full.prediction:
**Summary of News on the Death of Fabio Sementilli**

On January 23, 2017, Fabio Sementilli, a renowned hairdresser and executive at Coty Inc., was found dead in his Woodland Hills, Los Angeles home. The 49-year-old Canadian-born man was discovered by his wife and daughter on the patio of his gated residence, where he had been stabbed multiple times in the face, neck, and upper body. He was pronounced dead at the scene after paramedics arrived and found him bleeding profusely. The incident occurred in the upscale neighborhood of Woodland Hills, known for its security and affluent residents.

Homicide detectives from the Los Angeles Police Department (LAPD) were investigating the case, which remains under active inquiry. The police have not yet disclosed a motive for the attack. Sementilli’s black 2008 Porsche 911 Carrera, which was described as having paper license plates, was reported missing from his home. Detectives believe that two men may have broken into the house and fled in the vehicle.

The neighborhood, while generally quiet, has seen an increase in crime, according to some residents. Security cameras, including those from a local home across the street, were reportedly used in the investigation. The footage was reviewed by detectives, and the homeowner, Michael Geyer, stated that the video provided a timeline that could be helpful in the case.

Sementilli was a highly respected figure in the hairdressing industry, having served as vice president of education for Wella, a subsidiary of Coty Inc. He was known for his mentorship and leadership, often sharing motivational quotes and insights on leadership, integrity, and giving back to the community. His influence extended globally, and he was celebrated as an icon in the beauty and hair industry. Colleagues and friends, including Eden Sassoon, daughter of Vidal Sassoon, expressed deep sorrow over his death, calling him a mentor, friend, and a man who made a significant impact on the lives of many.

Sementilli’s passing has left a profound void in the industry, with many expressing their grief and admiration for his contributions. His legacy is remembered not only for his professional achievements but also for his positive attitude and commitment to mentoring others. The LAPD is urging anyone with information about the case to contact the Homicide Bureau at (818) 374-1925.
